destinations.name: Athirappilly – Vazhachal
destinations.tagline: Kerala's biggest waterfall and the Chalakudy river forests
destinations.description: Athirappilly Falls drops about 80 ft on the Chalakudy river at the edge of the Sholayar forests, with Vazhachal rapids 5 km upstream and Charpa Falls beside the road between them. The Vazhachal Forest Division runs the falls entry, guided treks from the falls entrance, and the Peringalkuthu–Karamthod forest trek; the riverine forest here is the only place in the Western Ghats where all four hornbill species are found together.
destinations.address: Office of the Divisional Forest Officer, Vazhachal Division, Chalakudy 680307
destinations.howToReach: About 30 km east of Chalakudy on the Athirappilly–Malakkappara road. Chalakudy railway station is the nearest (30 km); Thrissur 63 km; Kochi airport about 55 km (2–2.5 h). KSRTC and private buses run Chalakudy–Athirappilly all day; the Malakkappara bus continues past Vazhachal.
destinations.timings: Falls open 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Treks start 7:30 AM.

destinations.name: Peechi – Vazhani Wildlife Sanctuary
destinations.tagline: Trekking and coracle rides at Peechi dam, 20 km from Thrissur
destinations.description: A 125 sq km sanctuary set up in 1958 around the catchments of the Peechi and Vazhani dams, with moist deciduous and evergreen forest, more than 50 orchid species and over 240 birds. The Forest Department runs short and full-day guided treks from the Peechi dam side (Elephant Saga, Nasika, Dam Valley, Moodal Hill) and coracle rides on the reservoir, which can be combined into one ticket.

destinations.name: Chimmony Wildlife Sanctuary

destinations.name: Chulannur Peafowl Sanctuary
destinations.tagline: Mayiladumpara: dry forest, rock outcrops and dancing peacocks
destinations.description: A small 3.42 sq km sanctuary on the Thrissur–Palakkad border, known locally as Mayiladumpara, "the rock where peacocks dance". It is the only sanctuary in Kerala dedicated to the Indian peafowl and is dry deciduous country, so walks are short, open and best early in the morning. The Forest Department runs four guided treks graded from a two-hour stream walk to a six-hour, 8 km circuit.

programs.description: Located in Thrissur district, Kerala, Peechi-Vazhani Wildlife Sanctuary, established in 1958, is a sprawling 125 sq km expanse of moist deciduous, semi-evergreen, and evergreen forests. This vital catchment area for the Peechi and Vazhani dams is a biodiverse hotspot, home to over 50 species of orchids, rare medicinal plants, and diverse fauna including elephants, sambar deer, leopards, tigers, and over 240 bird species. Coracle Rides & Integrated Trekking Programs: Adding an exciting dimension to the sanctuary's offerings, coracle rides are now available directly at Peechi Dam, with options for both 20-minute and 40-minute durations. These traditional, bowl-shaped boats offer a unique, serene way to experience the reservoir and its surrounding forests from the water, providing excellent opportunities for quiet wildlife observation. Even more, these coracle rides can be combined with exhilarating trekking programs like "Elephant Saga" and "Nasika trail." This integration allows visitors to experience the sanctuary's diverse landscapes from both land and water, offering a comprehensive and immersive adventure that highlights the region's rich natural beauty and wildlife.

programs.description: Chulanoor Peafowl Sanctuary, spanning 3.42 sq km of dry deciduous forests, offers an ideal peafowl habitat. Witness mesmerizing peacock courtship dances, best seen early mornings or late afternoons. This biodiverse haven also shelters Grey Partridges, Spotted Doves, Indian Robins, Green Bee-eaters, White-browed Bulbuls, along with small mammals like hares and mongooses, and various reptiles. Post-monsoon, the sanctuary bursts with butterflies, enriching its natural charm. Facilities include a visitor center, observation points, and nature trails; carry your own snacks and water. Easily accessible by road, the sanctuary is near Palakkad Junction railway station and Coimbatore International Airport. For a responsible visit, wear comfortable shoes, bring binoculars and a camera, and respect wildlife by not feeding birds, maintaining silence, and avoiding litter. Immerse yourself in this tranquil sanctuary and experience the Indian Peafowl's unparalleled beauty, a testament to Kerala's conservation efforts.
